Indigenous research ethics knowledge sovereignty AIATSIS
searches.purpose: Locate plural international histories, first-generation programme and method accounts, independent criticism, a bounded Chinese empirical-accomplishment review, current institutions and an Indigenous-led research-ethics boundary while distinguishing indigenous psychologies developed within cultural settings from research about Indigenous Peoples, and while refusing to collapse Sikolohiyang Pilipino, Chinese/Taiwanese, Māori, Indian, Korean or other traditions into one culture

items.title: Origins and Development of Indigenous Psychologies: An International Analysis
items.rights_note: Publicly readable author-network copy reports contributors' accounts across multiple countries and global patterns; participant recollections and national summaries are heterogeneous and must not be rewritten as one origin, sequence or definition.

items.title: Indigenous and Cultural Psychology: Understanding People in Context
items.rights_note: Publicly readable publisher-identified volume contains programme statements, cross-Indigenous method discussion and internal debates; copyrighted body is private-cache only and the edited volume's chapters do not express one unanimous school position.

items.title: Indigenous Psychology, Westernized Psychology, and Indigenized Psychology: A Non-Western Psychologist's View
items.rights_note: Taiwan National Central Library record and bilingual abstract distinguishes indigenous, Westernized and indigenized psychology and indigenous compatibility; the article body is not treated as retrieved, and this Chinese-psychology framework is not imposed on all local traditions.

items.title: On the Rise and Decline of Indigenous Psychology
items.rights_note: Publisher record and abstract presents an external critique of definitional inconsistency, abstraction and universal-psychology proposals; restricted article body is not treated as read, and its strong decline thesis remains one contestable interpretation.
items.failure_note: The SAGE publisher abstract endpoint returned HTTP 403 to the collector; a Crossref DOI selection record was chosen without bypassing access controls.

items.title: Towards an Indigenous Chinese Psychology: A Selective Review of Methodological, Theoretical, and Empirical Accomplishments
items.rights_note: Chinese Journal of Psychology record and abstract reviews methodological, theoretical and empirical work in Taiwan, Hong Kong and mainland China; it is a selective participant review, not validation of all constructs or evidence about other indigenous psychologies.

items.title: Indigenous Psychology Network
items.rights_note: Current participant network documents continuing resources, calls and a plural mission for indigenous psychologies; an informal international network does not define accreditation, represent every local movement or resolve conceptual disputes.

items.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
items.rights_note: CC BY practice paper developed through Indigenous data-sovereignty networks defines Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility and Ethics; it governs Indigenous data rather than every aspect of psychology research, and the cached early proof's article-number placeholder must be resolved to final DOI 10.5334/dsj-2020-043.
items.failure_note: The preferred AIATSIS 2022 Code PDF and official landing page both returned HTTP 403 to the collector; the open CARE paper was selected as a global data and knowledge-sovereignty boundary without bypassing access controls.
